meta.seoDescription: Build cron jobs, health checks, and alerting workflows that keep your Minecraft infrastructure stable around the clock.

content.content: Automation lets a tiny volunteer crew support hundreds of players. This runbook compiles the scripts and checklists we trigger daily so free servers stay reliable without heroic effort.
We organise automation into four tracks: provisioning, backups, monitoring, and communication. Each track has a workflow diagram and a companion repository so you can fork and adapt the scripts.

All production nodes boot from the same Ansible playbook. Templates install Java, firewall rules, panel agents, and the latest Paper build. When we need a new world, a single command provisions the VM, attaches monitoring, and posts a Discord update in the staff channel.
Provisioning jobs log to a shared folder so we can audit changes. Every run also updates a Notion table that powers the status map on our website.

We run incremental backups every four hours and full snapshots nightly. A validation script spins up a disposable container, restores the latest snapshot, and runs `/tp` tours to ensure spawns load correctly.

- World archives live in object storage with 30-day retention.
- Snapshot metadata syncs to a Google Sheet so staff can request restores.
- Validation results ping a Discord webhook only when something fails so alerts stay actionable.
Pair these jobs with the [Designing a Backup Strategy](/blog/backup-strategy) article to build human-friendly recovery drills.

Prometheus scrapes JVM stats, disk usage, and network latency every 30 seconds. Grafana dashboards summarise the data for at-a-glance reviews, while Alertmanager routes urgent notifications to on-call volunteers.

| Signal | Threshold | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TPS | < 18 for 5 minutes | Trigger profiling workflow | 
| Disk usage | > 80% | Pause backups and notify storage lead |
| Packet loss | > 5% | Switch traffic through backup transit provider |
Alert noise kills trust, so we tag every notification with a follow-up task in Linear. Once the issue is resolved, the automation closes the ticket and posts a summary in #ops-changelog.

Automation should never feel mysterious. The runbook ships with communication templates so every script has a matching announcement. Scheduled jobs post summaries to Discord, and incident workflows create pre-filled threads where volunteers can coordinate.
Automation also powers transparency. Monthly reports combine donation snapshots, uptime percentages, and roadmap progress so the community can see the impact of each script they helped build.

content.title: Chain Automation with Other Playbooks
content.content: Layer the Automation Runbook with the [Performance Tuning Checklist](/blog/performance-tuning), the [Minecraft Server Security Checklist](/blog/security-checklist), and the [Community Hosting Blueprint](/blog/hosting-blueprint) to cover every side of operations.
